definition: Ostentatious means designed to impress others through an excessive, showy display, especially of wealth or importance.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ostentatious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ostentatious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The billionaire's ostentatious yacht came complete with a helicopter pad, a private cinema, and gold-plated bathroom fixtures.
A noticeable gold watch might catch someone's eye without seeming boastful — far short of ostentatious, which puts on a display designed to impress.
A showy gold watch draws deliberate attention to its own cost — one step short of ostentatious, which turns the whole display into a boast about wealth or importance.

Flashy emphasizes surface glitter — chrome, sequins, gold trim — appearance doing all the work. Ostentatious is about motive as much as look: an excessive display staged to impress others with wealth or importance. A flashy jacket may just be loud; an ostentatious one is a boast.

Pretentious means claiming a status one may not deserve — cultured, brilliant, important. Ostentatious is about the show of wealth or importance itself, deserved or not. A billionaire's gold-plated yacht is ostentatious but not pretentious; the money is real, the display is just excessive.

Extravagant means spending or consuming far beyond what is reasonable, and it needs no audience — you can be extravagant entirely in private. Ostentatious display exists to be seen: excess staged to impress others. Every ostentatious purchase is extravagant; a secret one can't be ostentatious.
